decisions.summary: Closing words Done / Superseded by / Withdrawn (case-insensitive prefix) in one tuple the tests import; Implemented is not a closing word; a task is a column-0 '- [ ]' / '- [x]' line, an indented box belongs to its task; no tasks = FILED.
decisions.why: FR-002 names finished/superseded/withdrawn and a once-stated set; the edge case says the tasks decide over an 'Implemented' status. Measured 2026-10-08 over specs/*/tasks.md: no tasks.md has all column-0 tasks ticked while holding an indented open box, so the indented-box rule hides no open work.

decisions.summary: scripts/speckit-todo.py run by make speckit-todo; three headed groups, one line per feature with title, ticked/total, (no spec.md) flag, counts per state; ALL=1 adds closed features with reason; exit 0 always.
decisions.why: FR-001, FR-003, FR-009 and the no-spec.md edge case. ALL=1 is opt-in and leaves the default listing exactly what FR-001 asks; it serves FR-004's audit.

decisions.summary: Status lines rewritten only with evidence in audit.md (Done (date): evidence / Superseded by NNN / Withdrawn (ruling, date)); mixed features keep open tasks open; unsettled ones stay open and are listed for the GM; tasks are not ticked.
decisions.why: FR-004 closes by editing the status line with recorded evidence; the spec's Assumptions keep unsettled features open for the GM.

decisions.summary: Search every spec and request for gm-assistant subjects and gm-assistant-only paths, read each hit, record search and result in audit.md, delete any found.

One make claim per filed entry; spec.md with heading title, Status 'Filed - from future-work/<file>, "<heading>", date', Input naming this feature, entry text verbatim; separate named pieces become one feature each; done or ruled-out entries closed in audit.md with evidence.

An entry naming an existing feature (the funerary-grounds entry, 'was feature 275, withdrawn') is filed INTO that feature's directory instead of under a newly claimed number, 'so one piece of work keeps one number'.
decisions.why: FR-006 requires every entry to become one NEW feature with its own claimed number (and the spec's Assumptions: numbers from make claim, one per filed feature). Nothing makes a new number impossible; 'one piece of work keeps one number' is a consistency/elegance argument, which does not legitimize an exception. It also cuts against the record: specs/275-*/request.md records the GM's withdrawal ('I think you can get rid of it entirely') and says 'The number stays spent; nothing is built under it', and the entry is wider than 275 (its heading adds 'and the headman's gate'). Reopening 275 rewrites a withdrawn feature's state rather than filing a new one. Fix: claim a new number for this entry like every other, and let its spec name 275 as its history.

decisions.summary: Re-aim every live future-work/ mention at the feature its entry became; directory-as-a-place mentions become the D7 rule; specs/, dev/*-log/, dev/review-ledger.md and hook fixtures keep their words as history; check-old-layout.py extended to fail a new live mention.
decisions.why: FR-007 and SC-004 say 'live'; FR-006 itself requires each filed spec to name the future-work file it came from, so specs/ cannot be swept; the project rule is that specs are history. Measured 2026-10-08: the only open feature mentioning future-work/ (130) names it as a path kind, not an entry. The check only fails when SC-004's requested state is absent - enforcement of the request, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md, dev/lessons.md and every doc saying 'add it to future-work' instead say: defer work by make claim + spec.md with Status Filed, find open work with make speckit-todo.
Conversion script kept in the spec directory; tests in tests/tooling/; baseline make done at cd33340f5, zero new failures.
decisions.why: Implementation placement and the constitution's regression rule; no scope change.
